habitat: Singly, in pairs or in small parties in woodland, fallow farmland and suburbia.
summary: A common resident. Grey-brown above, with a streaked crown, a bold white eyebrow, a stout blackish bill and white underparts, and no breast streaking. The song is a short rising wit-chee-chee-chee-cha phrase. While nest-building it repeats tweu, tweu, tirrirrit-tirik. The Kemp name is Steakyheaded Canary and the code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Forest Canary is heavily streaked yellow and has a small dark mask. Streaky-headed Seedeater is white below, with a streaked crown and a white eyebrow.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Streaked crown and a bold white eyebrow.

underparts.pattern: White below, with no breast streaking.

calls.description: A pleasant song in short bursts: wit-chee-chee-chee-cha, cha, cha, cha, cha, chip, rising to a crescendo. While nest-building it repeats tweu, tweu, tirrirrit-tirik. Grade A song from Grahamstown. The filename names Streaky-headed seedeater.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp name was left as Steakyheaded Canary. Population figures were left unchanged.
